items.title: Periodic responses of $\ddot z=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ and the affine classification of all solutions
items.reference: scaffold-added necessary mathematical prerequisite for the weak-field Thomson item (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
items.statement: Let $\omega>0$, $T:=2\pi/\omega$, $n\ge1$ and $w\in\mathbb C^n$; use the real part and complex exponential of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and [[def-complex-exponential]]. Define $z_p:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^n$ by $z_p(t):=\operatorname{Re}(-w\omega^{-2}e^{-i\omega t})$ componentwise ([[def-derivative]] for the derivative below). Then: (a) $z_p$ is $C^\infty$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) and satisfies $z_p''(t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$; it is $T$-periodic. (b) every $C^2$ solution $z:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^n$ of $z''(t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$ on $\mathbb R$ has the form $z(t)=z_p(t)+a+bt$ with unique $a,b\in\mathbb R^n$. (c) such a solution is $T$-periodic if and only if $b=0$; the $T$-periodic solutions are exactly $z_p(t)+a$, $a\in\mathbb R^n$, and their oscillating part has complex amplitude $-w/\omega^2$. (d) [Local solutions and exact global extension] Let I be any nonempty open interval, t* in I, and let z:I->R^n be C2 with the same harmonic equation on I. Then z=z_p+a+bt on I for a UNIQUE pair a,b, with b=z'(t*)-z_p'(t*) and a=z(t*)-z_p(t*)-bt*. The same explicit formula defines its unique global harmonic-ODE extension Z on R. This extension is T-periodic exactly when b0, equivalently z'(t*)=z_p'(t*); when b0 its mean over every complete period is a. For general drift, the mean of its global extension over [t,t+T] is a+b(t+T/2). Thus periodic preparation can be imposed on the global response without requiring a driven nonlinear family to exist on R. If I contains at least one pair t,t+T, equality at that pair forces b0. If I contains no such pair, a condition expressed only as z(t+T)=z(t) wherever both arguments belong to I is vacuous and does not imply periodicity of the global extension. All affine-drift local solutions remain classified, and the original global branches(a)-(c) remain intact.
items.strategy: (a) By the Cartesian form and Euler identity of [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], $z_p(t)=-\omega^{-2}[(\operatorname{Re}w)\cos(\omega t)+(\operatorname{Im}w)\sin(\omega t)]$ componentwise. Differentiating twice with the sum, scalar-multiple and product rules of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and the derivatives of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] gives $z_p''=\operatorname{Re}w\cos(\omega t)+\operatorname{Im}w\sin(\omega t)=\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})$. Periodicity of $z_p$ follows from $e^{-i\omega(t+T)}=e^{-i\omega t}e^{-i\omega T}=e^{-i\omega t}$ by the addition law of [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]] and $e^{-2\pi i}=1$, the latter from the Cartesian form and the values $\cos2\pi=1$, $\sin2\pi=0$ of [[thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period]]. (b) If $z$ is any $C^2$ solution, then $h:=z-z_p$ satisfies $h''=0$ on $\mathbb R$. Apply [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]] on the interval $\mathbb R$ ([[def-interval]]) to each component of $h'$: $h'=b$ is constant. Applying the same corollary to $h-b\,\mathrm{id}$ gives $h=a+bt$, and consequently $z=z_p+a+bt$. Uniqueness of $a,b$ from $z(0)$ and $z'(0)$ is immediate. (c) If $b=0$ then $z=z_p+a$ is $T$-periodic by (a). Conversely, if $z$ is $T$-periodic then $z(t+T)-z(t)=bT$ for all $t$, hence $b=0$; then $z-z_p=a$ is the constant part whose complex amplitude is zero, while the oscillating part $z_p$ has complex amplitude $-w/\omega^2$ by construction. No choice principle is used. For(d), apply the zero-derivative corollary on each closed subinterval of I to h'=z'-z_p', then to h-b id; any two points of the interval are contained in such a subinterval, so the constants agree throughout I. Evaluate at t* to get the displayed a,b, proving uniqueness. The explicit global formula is a solution on R by(a), and every other global solution extending z has the same value and derivative at t*, hence the same affine constants. Its period increment is bT, giving the periodicity equivalences and the single-pair test. Over every interval [t,t+T] the harmonic sine/cosine part has mean zero by scalar FTC. The affine part a+b s has mean a+b(t+T/2), since its integral is aT+b[(t+T)²-t²]/2. Therefore the global extension z_p+a+b s has mean a+b(t+T/2); it has mean a over EVERY complete period if and only if b=0. This last claim uses only ordinary finite-period integrals and no choice. The derivatives in(a) use the total chain rule [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] componentwise (or scalar coordinate-line chain rules), not a derivative rule asserted by the exponential definition alone.
